subject: Thomas Jefferson
overview: Thomas Jefferson was a Virginia planter, lawyer and politician who wrote the first draft of the Declaration of Independence and later became the third president of the United States, serving from 1801 to 1809. He also served as minister to France, as the first secretary of state and as vice president, and as president he doubled the size of the country with the Louisiana Purchase. He wrote that all men are created equal, yet over his lifetime he enslaved more than 600 people, a contradiction historians still argue over.

key_moments.title: Drafting the Declaration of Independence
key_moments.text: The **Second Continental Congress** named a **Committee of Five**, including **John Adams** and **Benjamin Franklin**, to draft a statement explaining why the colonies were breaking with Britain, and the committee gave the writing to the 33-year-old Jefferson. Congress then edited his draft heavily, cutting roughly a quarter of it, including a long passage blaming King George III for the slave trade. The **Declaration of Independence** was adopted on **July 4, 1776**, and Jefferson, who resented the cuts, sent friends copies of his original text so they could judge whether it had been improved or **mangled**.
claims: The Second Continental Congress appointed a Committee of Five, including Thomas Jefferson, John Adams and Benjamin Franklin, to draft the Declaration of Independence.
Thomas Jefferson wrote the first draft of the Declaration of Independence in 1776, at age 33.
Congress removed a passage from Thomas Jefferson's draft that condemned the slave trade.
The Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776.

key_moments.title: Religious freedom becomes Virginia law
key_moments.text: Jefferson drafted the **Virginia Statute for Religious Freedom** in 1777, declaring that no one could be forced to attend or pay for any church, but the Virginia legislature let it sit for years. It finally passed in **1786**, pushed through by his ally **James Madison**, while Jefferson himself was far away in Paris as American minister to France. The law became a model for the religion clauses of the **First Amendment**, and Jefferson ranked it among the three things he most wanted to be remembered for.
claims: Thomas Jefferson drafted the Virginia Statute for Religious Freedom in 1777.
The Virginia General Assembly enacted the Virginia Statute for Religious Freedom in 1786.
James Madison guided the Virginia Statute for Religious Freedom through the Virginia legislature.
Thomas Jefferson was serving as United States minister to France when the Virginia Statute for Religious Freedom passed.

key_moments.title: A tied election goes to the House
key_moments.text: In the **election of 1800** Jefferson defeated the sitting president, **John Adams**, but under the rules of the time electors cast two undifferentiated votes, and Jefferson tied with his own running mate, **Aaron Burr**. The deadlock went to the **House of Representatives**, which voted again and again before choosing Jefferson on the **36th ballot** in February 1801. The transfer of power between rival parties happened peacefully, and the mess led directly to the **Twelfth Amendment**, which made electors vote separately for president and vice president.
claims: Thomas Jefferson and Aaron Burr received the same number of electoral votes in the 1800 presidential election.
The House of Representatives chose Thomas Jefferson as president on the 36th ballot in February 1801.
The Twelfth Amendment, which required electors to cast separate votes for president and vice president, was adopted in response to the 1800 election tie.

key_moments.title: The Louisiana Purchase
key_moments.text: Jefferson sent envoys to Paris hoping to buy the port of **New Orleans**, and **Napoleon**, short of money and facing war with Britain, offered the whole **Louisiana territory** instead. The United States paid about **$15 million** for land that roughly **doubled the size of the country**, and Jefferson soon sent **Meriwether Lewis** and **William Clark** to explore it. The irony is that Jefferson, who had long argued for a strict reading of the Constitution, privately doubted the Constitution gave him the power to buy territory at all, and went ahead anyway.
claims: The United States bought the Louisiana territory from France in 1803 for about $15 million.
The Louisiana Purchase roughly doubled the size of the United States.
Thomas Jefferson doubted that the Constitution authorized the federal government to acquire new territory.
Thomas Jefferson commissioned the Lewis and Clark Expedition to explore the lands acquired in the Louisiana Purchase.

deep_facts.text: Jefferson and John Adams, once partners in independence and later bitter political rivals, reconciled in old age through a long exchange of letters. Both men then died on the same day: **July 4, 1826**, exactly fifty years after the Declaration of Independence was adopted. Adams, dying in Massachusetts, reportedly said that Thomas Jefferson still survived, not knowing that Jefferson had died at Monticello a few hours earlier.
claims: Thomas Jefferson and John Adams both died on July 4, 1826.
July 4, 1826 was the fiftieth anniversary of the adoption of the Declaration of Independence.
John Adams reportedly said that Thomas Jefferson survived, unaware that Jefferson had died hours earlier.

deep_facts.text: Jefferson designed his own grave marker, an obelisk, and wrote the inscription himself. It lists exactly three achievements: author of the Declaration of American Independence, author of the Statute of Virginia for religious freedom, and father of the University of Virginia. Two terms as **president of the United States**, along with his time as vice president and secretary of state, are not mentioned at all.
claims: Thomas Jefferson designed his own gravestone and wrote its epitaph.
Thomas Jefferson's epitaph names him as author of the Declaration of Independence, author of the Virginia Statute for Religious Freedom, and father of the University of Virginia.
Thomas Jefferson's epitaph does not mention his presidency.

deep_facts.text: Working with a razor and glue, Jefferson cut verses out of copies of the New Testament in several languages and pasted them into his own book, keeping the moral teachings of Jesus and leaving out the miracles and the resurrection. He titled it **The Life and Morals of Jesus of Nazareth** and kept it private. Today it is known as the **Jefferson Bible**, and in 1904 the US Congress printed an edition of it that was for decades handed to new members.
claims: Thomas Jefferson cut and pasted passages from the New Testament to create The Life and Morals of Jesus of Nazareth.
The Life and Morals of Jesus of Nazareth omits the miracles and the resurrection of Jesus.
The Life and Morals of Jesus of Nazareth is commonly known as the Jefferson Bible.
The United States Congress printed an edition of the Jefferson Bible in 1904.

connections.name: John Adams
connections.connection: Fellow Declaration committee member, later the rival he defeated in 1800, reconciled by letter before both died on July 4, 1826.

connections.name: James Madison
connections.connection: Closest political ally, co-founder of the Democratic-Republican Party, his secretary of state and his successor as president.

connections.name: United States Declaration of Independence
connections.connection: Jefferson wrote its first draft in 1776.

connections.name: Louisiana Purchase
connections.connection: Bought from France during his presidency in 1803, roughly doubling the United States.

connections.name: American Revolutionary War
connections.connection: Served as governor of Virginia during the war and fled Monticello ahead of British raiders in 1781.

connections.name: George Washington
connections.connection: Appointed Jefferson as the first United States secretary of state in 1789.

connections.name: Lewis and Clark Expedition
connections.connection: Jefferson commissioned the expedition to explore the Louisiana territory and reach the Pacific.

connections.name: Napoleon
connections.connection: Sold the Louisiana territory to Jefferson's government in 1803.

connections.name: First Barbary War
connections.connection: Jefferson sent the US Navy against the Barbary states rather than keep paying tribute to them.
